newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Asian Age
SYSTEM NEEDED TO DEAL WITH HUNG ASSEMBLIES

President Shanker Dayal Sharma called for developing healthy conventions to enable constitutional heads to function with due impartiality, independence and transparency while dealing with hung legislatures. Sharma made the observation at a high-powered conference held at his initiative to find answers to the ticklish issues thrown up by unclear verdicts in the lower house of parliament and state assembly polls. It was attended by governors, state chief ministers and leaders of various political parties.
Indian Express
PAWAR CITES BABRI, REFORMS IN HIS PLAN

Battle lines were formally drawn for the election of the Congress party president with Sharad Pawar announcing a major programme including a review of the economic policy. With Rajesh Pilot too sticking on, it is now formally a three-way contest, with current president Sitaram Kesri's name first on the ballot paper followed by Pawar's and Pilot's. The key elements of Pawar's policy for the future are a review of the economic policy and a meeting to denounce the demolition of the Babri mosque.
The Economic Times
US PENSION FUNDS BOOST FOREIGIN INVESTMENT STAKE IN BHEL

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have increased their holding in Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) by about four percentage points over the last one year to 16 percent. In one of the first cases where U.S. pension funds have invested in an Indian infrastructure company, Nynex Corporation Master Pension Trust and GT Service Corporation Pension Plan have picked up a stake in BHEL.
ABCL IN TALKS TO SELL STAKE

The Amitabh Bachchan Corporation (ABCL) is seeking a buyer to bail it out of its present financial mess. Amitabh Bachchan has begun negotiations with his erstwhile partner Ketan Somaiya to buy a substantial chunk of ABCL's equity. Bachchan is willing to sell up to 51 percent of the equity stake in ABCL to Somaiya. Arthur Anderson has been entrusted with the task of preparing a due diligence report, which has to tackle contentious issues such as the equity of the Bachchan brand.
BANKS ASKED TO FREEZE CRB CAPITAL'S ACCOUNTS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has asked banks to immediately instruct their branches to freeze the credit balances in the accounts of C.R. Bhansali of CRB Capital and his family members and other close relatives. This is in addition to the accounts of CRB Capital Markets and all other companies of the group. The RBI has provided banks with a list of CRB group companies whose accounts are to be immediately frozen. It has indicated that the list is not exhaustive, implying that if banks have suspicions, they may freeze the accounts on their own. The RBI list contains 36 names including CRB Capital Markets.
INDIA JOINS PACT GROUPING

India is entering into a sub-regional cooperation agreement with Thailand, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka to form a growth quadrangle to improve trade and investment flows between these countries. The development of such growth quadrangles can lead to an increase of at least 100 billion rupees to 150 billion rupees in exports from the country. Investments, too, will be easier to find since linkages between countries will be closer in the case of sub-regional groupings, say analysts.
Financial Express
40 CRB GROUP SHARES DECLARED AS BAD DELIVERIES

The Bombay bourse has informed its investors that shares of all the 40 companies linked to the CRB group will be treated as bad delivery with immediate effect. The exchange will consider measures against members instrumental in delivering such shares in the market. It is for the first time since the multi-billion stocks and securities scam of 1992, that the country's premier bourse has decided to treat as bad delivery shares of such a large number of companies linked to any particular group. It is expected that all the bourses in the country where shares of any of these companies are listed will be treated as bad delivery.
UNIT TRUST TAKES MAURITIUS ROUTE FOR DEBT FUND

Unit Trust of India (UTI) has set up a Mauritius-based company to kick off its maiden $150 million India Debt Fund (IDF). Nomura International of London, the European arm of the Japanese investment banking major, will act as the manager of the fund. Road shows for the IDF will be kicked off by three executives from UTI. A new Mauritius-based company named India Debt Fund Limited has been set up in Mauritius.
PLANS TO OFFER LOANS AND BROKERAGE FOR FIXED DEPOSITS

The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) is planning a concerted attack on the fixed deposit market by offering loans against deposits, premature withdrawal facilities and paying brokerage. At present the institutions cannot offer loans against deposits.This makes their fixed deposits less attractive than those of the banks. They plan to move the Reserve Bank on these issues, says IDBI chairman. He said banks have certain advantages over the institutions and the people do not go to banks merely to earn interest. The IBDI has also chalked out plans to storm the fixed deposit market by offering a one percent brokerage besides the offered interest rate.
Business Standard
$15 BLN PROJECTS TO BE OFFERED TO U.S. INVESTORS

Projects valued at over $15 billion in power, petroleum, telecom, roads, civil aviation and ports sectors will be offered to American investors during the visit of an Indian delegation. The delegation will hold a series of meetings with American companies and investors. The government is working to tie-up several loose ends in the policy framework in sectors like power to ensure that there are no impediments to foreign direct investments. The projects to be offered include oil pipelines, highways, ports, coal mining and power projects with six in transmission networks totalling $2.3 billion and a 1,000 mw coal-based project, four refinery projects.
POLICY CHANGE KEY TO HIGHER SAVINGS, SAYS IMF

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has discounted the efficacy of traditional tax and interest rate incentives as a means to boost savings in the economy. Instead, it has backed a programme of financial liberalisation. According to a study carried out in the Fund's publication, a sustained increase in long term savings will require two major policy changes. First, the government will have to sharply reduce its recourse to captive financing from pension funds and Life Insurance Corporation. Secondly, greater private sector involvement will be required to boost competition and more innovative product development.
RANGARAJAN SIGNALS LOW INTEREST RATE REGIME

The Reserve Bank governor urged banks to reduce their spreads and keep interest rates low for borrowers, signalling a low interest rate regime. The governor's statement assumes significance after some institutions said cost of funds has been moving upwards. The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation has stated that lending rates may have to be hiked if the cost of liabilities goes above 12 percent at the short end. Industrial Development Bank too is facing resistance from investors for its 13.5 percent five-year paper. The governor said the monetary policy will be supportive in bringing down interest rates.
The Observer
LIQUEFIED NATURAL GAS PROJECT DETAILS REVIEWED

The Petroleum and Natural Gas secretary reviewed and evaluated two tenders received for a feasibility report to design the proposed liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal and several offer bids from LNG suppliers. While 50 percent of the equity of 12 billion rupees will be held by the participating companies, the remaining 50 percent will be offered to financial institutions, multilateral agencies and the like. It has been decided to set up one LNG import facility each in the states of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Gujarat. Each of these four LNG terminals will have a start-up capacity of 2.5 million tonnes a year with a provision for expansion up to five million tonnes a year.
BULK IMPORT OF UNSORTED WASTE PAPER URGED

A report has recommended the government to permit bulk imports of unsorted waste paper for sorting in India for use by domestic industry and for re-export. The report said bulk imports will mean lower ocean freight, creation of new jobs for sorting and baling, the possibility of setting up economy-sized plants based on waste paper and the stimulation of an organised collection and sorting system. To facilitate imports, the government should abolish customs duty on import of waste paper and pulp. It can also help the industry in creating national warehouses, sorting and baling facility to collect domestic waste paper and to sort imported waste paper in bulk.
SPECIAL SCHEME TO IMPORT RAW MATERIAL FOR GARMENTS

The government is working on a special scheme to allow garment exporters to import raw material for the first time in a bid to push up value addition in price. The Textiles Ministry is sympathetic to the demand to allow such imports, including that of high class fibre. The scheme is being worked out and may be announced soon. The new scheme may take into consideration a suggestion that garment exporters be allowed to import up to two percent of their export earnings in the previous year, raw materials, consumables and accessories, without any import duty and without any import licence.
